dense._note: Arm D is RE-MEASURED global DINOv2-small ridge (never quoted from M107), at resolutions whose MACs sit at-or-above the routed specialists' per-image cost; the t1 gate requires it to reproduce M107/M109 t1.
dense.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens

device._note: Sparse whitening stays on numpy CPU (M107's arithmetic); encode + distance on the GPU ('cuda' = ROCm/HIP). HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1, device_count 1, gcnArchName gfx1201.

gate._comparison_rule: a routed per-domain Arm P prediction costs router + one specialist per input; Arm D is compared at the resolution whose per-image MACs are at-or-above that total (never below, so the sparse side cannot win by being cheaper).
gate.kill_switch_1_ceiling_lift: if oracle-routed per-domain Arm P does not beat the global frozen dictionary (0.2148) overall by at least 0.01, routing does not lift the sparse ceiling and the routed idea adds nothing beyond M109; the program consolidates.
gate.kill_switch_2_vs_dense: if oracle-routed Arm P beats Arm D at-or-above its cost on any domain, routed sparse specialists beat a trained transformer per-domain at matched cost (the only measured regime where the program's sparse family wins on accuracy).
gate.registered_prediction: routing lifts the frozen sparse ceiling modestly on non-natural domains (quickdraw, sketch, clipart) but does not reach the dense model's accuracy.

head._note: per A2 (sealed): the closed-form ridge head, never a trained linear head, on sparse codes.

parity_guard.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens

fingerprint._note: the oracle router (true test domain labels) is the primary control and carries the family verdicts; the fingerprint router's routing accuracy is reported as a gate beside every routed figure.
fingerprint.descriptor: per-image mean and std of raw pixels

sparse._atoms_note: floor-capped: atoms_d = floor(D_d / 44.92) where D_d is the domain's train rows and 44.92 = 4 * 11.23 (the section 3.5 floor), so each specialist keeps >= 11.23 rows per fitted dimension. Computed at registration.
sparse._floor_repair: REGISTERED REPAIR, 8 August 2026, before any re-run. First sealed run (a5_routed.json as registered) SELF-VOIDED on the per-domain floor gate: d1 was registered at 258 atoms but floor(11587/44.92) = 257.947, cap 257, so 258 exceeded the floor by 1. Corrected 258 -> 257. All other domains verified: {249, 361, 945, 907, 350} are each <= floor(D_d/44.92). The runner also now fits every head on ALL train rows (no vestigial 5% validation split - A5 has no SGD and selects no hyperparameter), matching M107's dense arm and per-domain mixture arm, so the recorded rows-per-fitted-dimension agrees with the floor gate. Registration: analysis/RESEARCH_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_v17.md, A5 section.
sparse.dictionary_per_domain: random whitened-patch sample restricted to that domain's train rows (M108 arm (a) construction, domain-specific)
sparse.whitener: global M108 (fitted on the full subsample)
